title: "Projects"
subtitle: "The sidebar: every folder you work in, with every session in it, from both agents."

{{< include _sk/projects.html >}}

## Projects {.i-folder}

A project is a folder you have run an agent in. The sidebar lists them
all, the newest first, pinned ones on top. Click a project to unfold its
sessions. The plus on its row starts a new session there ([⌘T]{.kbd} in
the project you are in, [⌘N]{.kbd} anywhere). A project with a live
session wears the accent and opens by itself.

Right-click a project to archive or delete its sessions, open it in
Finder, or hide it. Hidden projects and the system's temporary folders
sit under their own headings at the foot. Nothing in a project's own
folder is ever touched.

## Sessions {.i-scroll}

Each session is a row under its project: the agent's mark, lit while it
runs, a dot for where it stands, the title, and a bar at the left when it
has a tab. Claude Code and Codex sessions sit side by side, each read
from its own files.

**All Sessions** ([⌘L]{.kbd}) lists every project and every session with
the day it was last touched, archived ones under their own heading, and
narrows to one agent. Select many at once ([⌘]{.kbd}-click,
[⇧]{.kbd}-click, or drag a rectangle), then archive or delete them
together.

## Kept and archived {.i-archive}

Claude Code deletes its transcripts after thirty days. Emaki copies every
one into `~/.emaki/archive` the first time it sees it, so a session the
agent has deleted is still listed, searchable and readable, marked
*kept*. Codex deletes nothing by age, so its sessions are read in place.

*Archive* a session and the agent leaves it alone until you unarchive it.
*Delete* moves every copy to the Trash. Renaming a session renames it for
the agent too.

## Search {.i-search}

[⌘K]{.kbd} searches every session on the machine. One hit per prompt,
paragraph, thought or tool call, so a hit lands on the thing you
remembered, in live and kept sessions alike.

## Tabs {.i-copy}

Every open session is a tab, grouped by project. [⌘1]{.kbd} to
[⌘9]{.kbd} switch, [⌘W]{.kbd} closes, [⌘⇧T]{.kbd} brings back the last
one closed, and a drag reorders them.
